enhancement.text: 1-ID uses very high-energy X-rays, about 40–140 keV (thousand electron-volts), that pass through centimetres of metal to map stress and crystal grains inside engine parts and batteries. The plan replaces its bent-crystal monochromator – two bent silicon crystals that select one X-ray energy – with one turned on its side, deflecting the beam sideways rather than upwards because the new ring’s source is smallest in the vertical plane, where an upward-deflecting crystal would blur it; it also gives 1-ID-C a new sample-handling and detector system. Status (2026): the 1-ID-C system has been delivered and 1-ID-E keeps its pre-upgrade setup; the new monochromator and the planned superconducting undulator are not confirmed as installed.

beamlines.summary: Maps where trace metals sit inside frozen cells and materials with a 50–200 nm X-ray spot.

enhancement.text: 2-ID makes X-ray ‘element maps’ of cells, soils and microchips by scanning a tiny spot across the sample and recording the fluorescence – X-rays of a characteristic energy that each element gives off. The plan adds a focusing mirror to each branch that re-images the source onto a fixed aperture, a steady stand-in source that tolerates the 2.5-fold change in vertical source size between operating modes; replaces the zone-plate lenses of 2-ID-E with Kirkpatrick–Baez (KB) mirrors, which deliver 60–80% of the X-rays instead of 10–20%; and builds a frozen-sample nanoprobe, Bionanoprobe-II, aiming for 10-nanometre detail. Status (2026): Bionanoprobe-II is under construction, and 2-ID-E still runs with zone plates.

beamlines.name: 3-ID-B,C,D
beamlines.title: 3-ID-B,C,D: Nuclear Resonant Scattering (NRS)
beamlines.summary: Tunes X-rays to make atomic nuclei (⁵⁷Fe, ⁸³Kr, ¹⁵¹Eu, ¹⁶¹Dy) resonate, revealing atomic vibrations and magnetism, even at deep-Earth pressures.
beamlines.operator: XSD Inelastic X-ray & Nuclear Resonant Scattering (IXN)
techniques: nuclear resonant scattering (NRIXS/NRVS, NFS, synchrotron Mossbauer)

enhancement.text: 3-ID tunes X-rays so precisely – to about a thousandth of an electron-volt out of 14,400, better than one part in ten million – that they make the nuclei of particular isotopes such as iron-57 resonate, revealing how atoms vibrate inside rocks squeezed to deep-Earth pressures or inside enzymes. The upgrade added Kirkpatrick–Baez (KB) focusing mirrors that shrink the beam from about 20 µm to about 1 µm, so tiny samples in diamond-anvil pressure cells can be measured. Status (2026): the focusing is in use – about 1.5 × 12 µm (horizontal × vertical) with the iron-57 monochromator – while a planned, funding-dependent new cryogenic monochromator has not been confirmed.
fdrDeliverables: (operating funds) relocation of IXS spectrometer to 3-ID-D
enhancement.asBuilt: 2026 directory: micro-focusing in 3-ID-B and 3-ID-C to ~1 x 1 um^2 or 1 x 12 um^2; HRMs for 57Fe (1 meV at 14.4 keV), 83Kr, 151Eu, 161Dy; cryo-cooled Si(111) HHLM 7-27 keV; 3-ID-D now 'nuclear resonant scattering with dual fast shutter system' and 'instrument development' (no IXS spectrometer listed). SEES (May 2025): 57Fe NRIXS/NFS available with a 1.5 x 12 um (H x V) focus; ~10 x 10 um planned for Kr/Eu/Dy. An energy-domain Mossbauer spectrometer was under development for late 2025. Undulators installed are 2.7 cm (not the FDR 2.5 cm).
enhancement.deliveryStatus: KB focusing delivered (1-1.5 um H); ~12 um vertical with the 57Fe HRM suggests the dispersion-compensated HRM is not in place (inference); IXS relocation not evidenced

beamlines.notes: Directory techniques still include 'Inelastic x-ray scattering (1 meV resolution)', but no IXS endstation is listed; 3-ID-D is now an NRS/instrument-development station.

enhancement.text: Sector 6 studies magnetism and atomic order in crystals. The upgrade split its straight section into two independent X-ray beams angled 1 milliradian apart (‘canting’), so 6-ID-B/C and 6-ID-D can run at once. The plan also adds compound refractive lenses – stacks of tiny curved lenses, each bending X-rays only slightly – in beryllium to focus 6-ID-B/C below a micrometre, and in aluminium for high-energy 6-ID-D, where a test at 60 keV gave a 50 × 3.7 µm spot. Status (2026): both canted beams are in user operation, fed by permanent-magnet undulators rather than the planned superconducting one; installation of the lenses has not been announced.

enhancement.text: 7-ID makes ‘stop-motion movies’ of materials: a laser flash starts a change and an X-ray flash, a precisely timed moment later, records it. Status (2026): delivered, and the general user program has fully resumed.

enhancement.text: 27-ID does resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS): it measures the tiny amounts of energy X-rays lose when they stir up electrons and their magnetism in quantum materials. Some of its spectrometer’s motion stages were more than 30 years old, and the point where all its rotation axes should meet wandered by about 200 µm (two or three hair widths); the rebuild was designed to hold it within 5 µm, separates the sample motions from the detector arm and leaves room for bigger sample environments. It was the first APS-U enhancement to be finished, in March 2022 – before the old ring shut down.
enhancement.asBuilt: APS News (Aug 2022): enhanced spectrometer and high-resolution monochromator online in March 2022 - 'the first available beamline enhancement funded by the APS Upgrade Project'; sample and analyzer motions decoupled; more room for in situ/operando environments; designed to accept quartz curved and flat-crystal ultra-high-resolution optics. 2026 directory: 5-14 keV, 10-200 meV, focus 10 x 10 um.
